newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cable TV networks target Latin America - NYT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cable TV networks target Latin America - NYT.

text.p: Latin America has turned into a battleground for U.S. cable television networks vying against local rivals for viewers, according to the New York Times in its Monday edition.

Rising incomes, the introduction of satellite dishes and the proliferation of 24-hour news services have attracted cable television to Latin America, where a pay-television market is expected to generate at least $2.5 billion annually in advertising revenue and subscriber fees by 2000.

"We feel the marketplace has matured to the point that a 24-hour-a-day operation makes sense both journalistically and financially," Eason Jordan, executive vice president of International CNN, a unit of Time Warner Inc, was quoted as saying.

"Latin America is an awfully big place, where the cable and satellite market places are growing extraordinarily rapidly, advances in technology and systems of distribution have created new opportunities, and most countries, with the notable exception of Brazil, speak the same language," Jordan added.

A study published in April by Audits and Surveys, a New York media research company, showed that the number of households in Latin America with cable or satellite television rose last year to 14.2 million from 10.9 million in 1995.
CNN en Espanol went on the air on March 17 and it is not alone.

Westinghouse Electric Corp's CBS has been in the market for nearly a year after buying Telenoticias in mid-1996 from a consortium that included Reuters Holdings Plc, Telemundo Group Inc and the Antena 3 network of Spain.
